chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from his father, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'If four men testified before me against a man for adultery, and among them was a son of adultery (walad al-zina), I would administer the punishment (hadd) to all of them, because his testimony is not valid and he do not lead the people (in prayer).'

key_terms.لَحَدَدْتُهُمْ: I would administer the fixed punishment (hadd) to them
key_terms.وَلَدُ زِنًى: Son of adultery (a specific category of person with distinct legal rulings)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a walad al-zina regarding witness testimony and leading prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a 'son of adultery' (walad al-zina) is disqualified from being a witness in court and from leading others in prayer. Consequently, if four such individuals testify against someone for adultery, their testimony is invalid, and they themselves are subject to the hadd punishment.
